source_text: Ais iterum et dicis: Nulla esset concupiscentia, nisi homo ante peccasset, nuptiae vero essent, etiamsi nemo peccasset
pass_a_gloss: You say again and you say: There would be no desire unless the human being had first sinned, but marriages would exist even if no one had sinned.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: Again you say: “There would be no desire if the human being had not first sinned, but marriage would exist even if no one had sinned.”

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian excerpt in the intermediary document
